area: Homepage and public navigation
title: First useful demo action is below the first phone screen
observation: At 390×844 the initial viewport ends in the demo contact header; the draft and its actions are further down.
recommendation: Shorten the mobile introduction or make Try the demo land on the first editable action.
acceptance: A new visitor reaches a draft with one deliberate tap without hunting through contact fields.

area: Homepage and public navigation
title: Two acquisition tasks compete for attention
observation: The header, hero and demo repeat waitlist actions while the product asks the visitor to try an example.
recommendation: Choose a primary action for each stage and use a clear progression from example to access request.
acceptance: In a moderated task, visitors can explain what each action does before choosing it.

area: Homepage and public navigation
title: Useful navigation disappears on phones
observation: PublicHeader hides Templates/Questions section links on narrow screens and relies on the footer.
recommendation: Provide a compact public menu or a visible secondary navigation row.
acceptance: Templates and Questions remain reachable near the top at 320 and 390 pixels.

area: Homepage and public navigation
title: Free access is explained late
observation: The free-account/no-card explanation is in the closing waitlist section, away from the first signup actions.
recommendation: Place concise, verified access and price expectations next to the initial waitlist CTA.
acceptance: Users understand that a request joins a queue rather than opens an account immediately.

area: Homepage and public navigation
title: The roadmap is not current launch evidence
observation: The roadmap contains checked sandbox and continuity criteria that conflict with current source and live behavior. No customer-comprehension study was run in this audit.
recommendation: Reconcile checked items against this build and run the supplied research protocol with actual target users.
acceptance: Every completed roadmap item links to current evidence; research results are separated from planning hypotheses.

area: Profession pages — shared findings apply to all five
title: Primary waitlist links drop profession context
observation: Hero, header and demo links go to /waitlist without a scenario. Only the embedded bottom form supplies persona.id.
recommendation: Carry an allowlisted profession through every waitlist entry point.
acceptance: Each page’s top, demo and bottom CTAs preserve the same intended onboarding context.

area: Profession pages — shared findings apply to all five
title: Selected Mix is not carried into signup
observation: ProductDemo changes its own scenario state, but its waitlist link is generic and it does not dispatch the scenario event consumed by WaitlistForm.
recommendation: Define a supported mapping from the chosen example to the starter and persist it at request time.
acceptance: Selecting a nondefault example survives invitation redemption in a fresh browser.

area: Profession pages — shared findings apply to all five
title: The phone experience delays the professional example
observation: All five reuse the long hero-before-demo stack; visitors first read positioning and selectors.
recommendation: Bring the profession-specific draft or a compact preview closer to the opening claim.
acceptance: A visitor can identify the example’s person, reason and next step in the first short interaction.

area: Profession pages — shared findings apply to all five
title: Tool-boundary clarification comes after the demo
observation: What the app does not replace is in a lower section; visitors may assume a CRM, ATS, quoting or booking integration.
recommendation: Place the most relevant limitation beside the first example, with the fuller explanation below.
acceptance: A recruiter, consultant, photographer, agent or contractor can correctly describe the supported workflow.

area: Profession pages — shared findings apply to all five
title: Profession fit remains an untested hypothesis
observation: The five ICPs explicitly describe fictional composites. Working pages and tailored text do not establish usefulness or conversion.
recommendation: Test one real follow-up task per profession; retain observed errors and language rather than fictional quotations.
acceptance: Each profession has task-completion and comprehension evidence before claims of validated fit.

area: Interactive public demo
title: Changing examples silently discards edited messages
observation: Edited Lead to a sentinel, switched to Quote and back; the original message returned. Completion state survives, creating inconsistent persistence.
recommendation: Keep each scenario’s draft in memory, or ask before discarding it.
acceptance: Message, subject and planned date survive switching away and back.

area: Interactive public demo
title: A public practice session offers real communication-app handoffs
observation: The live demo exposes sms/mailto/tel actions and editable recipient details; this differs from the roadmap’s sandbox contract.
recommendation: Choose and document the intended contract. Prefer a fictional preview and explicit simulated result.
acceptance: Demo completion never opens an external composer under a sandbox promise.

area: Interactive public demo
title: Icon-only completion is hard to distinguish from sending
observation: A checkmark sits beside the native-app action and Skip, without a persistent visible explanation of simulated completion.
recommendation: Label the completion control and show a short result that explains what was recorded.
acceptance: Participants distinguish opening, sending, recording and skipping without assistance.

area: Interactive public demo
title: Attachment language exceeds what the demo prepares
observation: The consultant proposal example says the proposal is attached, while the mailto handoff supplies subject and body only.
recommendation: Remove the attachment assertion or display an explicit reminder to attach the document in the mail app.
acceptance: No draft asserts an attachment is present unless the user has supplied it.

area: Interactive public demo
title: Planned timing sounds like automatic sending
observation: The date hint says the date this beat goes out, although the primary demo handoff is manual.
recommendation: Use scheduled-to-appear/review wording and separate it from the user’s actual sending time.
acceptance: Visitors correctly explain that selecting a date does not send a message.

area: Interactive public demo
title: Reset behavior is fragmented
observation: Use sample contact resets contact values; Use prepared message resets one draft; completed/skipped state has separate controls.
recommendation: Provide an explicit reset-example action with a clear scope.
acceptance: A visitor can return the entire current example to its initial state in one action.

area: Public templates, reminders, FAQ and trust pages
title: Public templates and saved Mixes have similar names
observation: Public navigation says Templates, while the account library is Ready-made mixes; one is editorial content and one creates plans.
recommendation: Explain the difference at the public library entry and use consistent transition labels.
acceptance: Visitors know whether a CTA copies example text, previews a workflow, or requests account access.

area: Public templates, reminders, FAQ and trust pages
title: Long reference pages need stronger navigation
observation: FAQ and policy pages are lengthy reading tasks; the main acquisition/navigation actions do not help locate a specific topic.
recommendation: Add a concise contents list and stable anchors for account access, data, sending and support.
acceptance: A user reaches a named topic without scanning the whole document on a phone.

area: Public templates, reminders, FAQ and trust pages
title: Recovery help is disconnected from failed actions
observation: The public contact page exists, but several auth errors refer to the site operator without linking to it.
recommendation: Reuse a public support link and a concise recovery explanation in error states.
acceptance: A signed-out user can reach working support directly from every account-recovery failure.

area: Public templates, reminders, FAQ and trust pages
title: Educational claims lack a visible capability summary
observation: Manual sending, optional automatic delivery, reminders and external apps are explained in separate places.
recommendation: Add a short shared capability summary with links to deeper explanations.
acceptance: The template, reminder and FAQ pages describe the same current sending contract.

area: Public templates, reminders, FAQ and trust pages
title: Trust content needs an owner-led factual review
observation: This audit inspected presentation and current copy, not the legal adequacy or completeness of policies.
recommendation: Have the responsible owner reconcile policies with actual retention, support and provider behavior.
acceptance: Record a dated content review and resolve any mismatched product claims before broad release.

area: Waitlist, invitation entry and confirmation recovery
title: Joining and confirming are not explained before submission
observation: The opening promise emphasizes being emailed when it is the user’s turn; confirmation is chiefly explained in the receipt.
recommendation: Show a brief request → confirm email → await invitation sequence.
acceptance: A first-time visitor knows to look for and act on the confirmation email.

area: Waitlist, invitation entry and confirmation recovery
title: Submitted form retains the initial action label
observation: WaitlistForm shows a submitted message but continues to render Join the waitlist rather than an explicit resend/change-address state.
recommendation: Make next actions explicit while preserving the generic, non-enumerating receipt.
acceptance: Repeat submissions clearly distinguish changing an address from requesting another confirmation.

area: Waitlist, invitation entry and confirmation recovery
title: Error text is not associated with the email control
observation: The input gets aria-invalid, but the error paragraph has no ID referenced by aria-describedby or aria-errormessage.
recommendation: Associate validation text with its field and focus an actionable error summary when needed.
acceptance: A screen-reader user hears the specific error when returning to the email field.

area: Waitlist, invitation entry and confirmation recovery
title: Unavailable invitations have a broad fallback
observation: Invalid, revoked and used links share a message and waitlist CTA. A legitimate invited person can mistake this for a need to restart access.
recommendation: Keep the privacy-safe response but add clear sign-in and request-help choices.
acceptance: A user with a previously used link can recover without mistakenly joining the queue again.

area: Waitlist, invitation entry and confirmation recovery
title: Temporary pauses have weak recovery expectations
observation: Paused signup asks users to reopen the same link later, without a support route or a specific way to check availability.
recommendation: Explain which step is paused and link to public help; avoid invented reopening dates.
acceptance: The user knows the link remains usable and has a useful action during the pause.

area: Sign-in, password recovery and verification
title: Password fields have no visibility toggle
observation: Sign-in, registration and reset render password inputs without a reveal control.
recommendation: Add accessible show/hide controls without changing password-manager support.
acceptance: Users can inspect and correct a long password on mobile and with a keyboard.

area: Sign-in, password recovery and verification
title: Authentication submits lack pending feedback
observation: These server-action forms use ordinary submit buttons without a pending label or disabled state.
recommendation: Use the existing FormSubmitButton pattern on authentication actions.
acceptance: Slow requests visibly enter a pending state and cannot be accidentally resubmitted.

area: Sign-in, password recovery and verification
title: Validation returns page-level errors
observation: Errors are passed in redirects and displayed above the form; fields lack error associations and nonsecret values are not consistently restored.
recommendation: Preserve name/email and associate specific errors, while clearing sensitive passwords deliberately.
acceptance: A failed signup or reset can be corrected without re-entering unrelated nonsecret information.

area: Sign-in, password recovery and verification
title: Recovery copy exposes implementation language
observation: Forgot password explains account-enumeration behavior and refers to an installation/site operator.
recommendation: Use simple recovery instructions with a public contact link; retain the security behavior in code.
acceptance: A customer can understand the next step without knowing how the site is hosted.

area: Sign-in, password recovery and verification
title: Protected destination is lost after sign-in
observation: loginAction chooses Today or onboarding through accountHome rather than retaining the originally requested customer route.
recommendation: Carry a validated same-origin return path through sign-in.
acceptance: Following a contact or support-ticket link while signed out returns to that item after authentication.

area: Onboarding and first useful action
title: Success is announced for a person who cannot be reached
observation: Submitted a name without phone/email. The next screen said the first follow-up was ready, but its primary action was Add phone.
recommendation: Require a method appropriate to the selected first beat, or explicitly offer a notes-only setup with accurate success copy.
acceptance: A ready-to-send success state has a usable recipient; incomplete records receive an honest next step.

area: Onboarding and first useful action
title: Default date uses UTC instead of the account timezone
observation: onboarding/page.tsx sets today with toISOString().slice(0,10), while follow-ups use the selected local timezone. Near UTC midnight these are different dates.
recommendation: Derive the initial logical date in the user’s selected timezone.
acceptance: At 01:00 UTC, a Los Angeles user receives the preceding local date; test both sides of midnight.

area: Onboarding and first useful action
title: The one-person start is a long setup form
observation: The 390-pixel page measured 2,768 pixels high and contains four sections before the first result.
recommendation: Reduce the initial path to person, relevant context and timing; defer optional business configuration.
acceptance: A novice completes the first useful follow-up with minimal scrolling and can skip optional setup visibly.

area: Onboarding and first useful action
title: Business name remains required on the default path
observation: Business is preselected, and businessName is required before a first follow-up can be prepared.
recommendation: Support a minimal first action with a personal signature and allow business details later.
acceptance: A business user can prepare a personal follow-up before completing the business profile.

area: Onboarding and first useful action
title: Starter assignment is not reviewable before creation
observation: The form selects a reason but gives only a generic what-happens-next paragraph, rather than the actual messages, channels and dates.
recommendation: Preview the chosen starter and permit change/skip before assignment.
acceptance: Users see the complete first plan and explicitly accept its timing before it is created.

area: Onboarding and first useful action
title: Referrals interrupt the first-success screen
observation: The welcome screen places Prepare invitations above Today and the first customer follow-up.
recommendation: Prioritize completing the requested follow-up; offer invitations after that useful action.
acceptance: The first screen after setup makes the chosen person’s next action visually primary.

area: Onboarding and first useful action
title: Import requires cross-tab coordination
observation: Onboarding opens import in a new tab and asks the user to return and press Refresh imported contacts.
recommendation: Use a clear return-to-setup link and refresh the saved-contact choices on return.
acceptance: A successful import yields a selectable person without guessing which tab or refresh control to use.

area: Workspace navigation, Quick Add and voice capture
title: Calendar and journey are several steps from daily work
observation: Primary navigation is Today, Contacts, Mixes and More; calendar/journey are secondary destinations.
recommendation: Test a task-based shortcut or configurable frequent destinations.
acceptance: Regular users reach their frequent scheduling and relationship tasks predictably from any page.

area: Workspace navigation, Quick Add and voice capture
title: Journey highlights a different parent than its entry point
observation: More links to Customer journey, but Nav marks Contacts active on /journey.
recommendation: Use consistent navigation ancestry or show an explicit relationship between the destinations.
acceptance: Entering journey from More does not unexpectedly change the perceived navigation section.

area: Workspace navigation, Quick Add and voice capture
title: Several More labels describe unrelated tasks together
observation: More, Settings, Profile and My Account overlap in where people expect to find preferences and security.
recommendation: Use a single task taxonomy and consistent labels across desktop and mobile.
acceptance: Users find timezone, notifications and sign-out without opening multiple menus.

area: Workspace navigation, Quick Add and voice capture
title: Quick Add transfer is temporary and lost on reload
observation: NewContactForm consumes a capture draft once and explicitly warns that reload clears it.
recommendation: Offer a recoverable account-scoped draft or an explicit save-draft step, subject to existing privacy boundaries.
acceptance: A routine refresh during review does not erase a captured note unexpectedly.

area: Workspace navigation, Quick Add and voice capture
title: Voice and native contact capture need device qualification
observation: The audit used Chromium and synthetic fixtures; it did not exercise real microphones or the physical contact picker.
recommendation: Run the existing physical-device protocol for permission denial, interruption, language and unsupported-browser fallback.
acceptance: Record actual iPhone/Android outcomes, including recovery without losing typed text.

area: Today list and follow-up discovery
title: Today has no person or message search
observation: Filters cover dates, status and method, but the list has no search field.
recommendation: Add scoped person/Mix search that preserves filter and pagination context.
acceptance: A user can find a named person’s due beat without paging through unrelated follow-ups.

area: Today list and follow-up discovery
title: Repeated plan and reason text adds noise
observation: Seeded cards display combinations such as Estimate follow-up · Estimate follow-up.
recommendation: Deduplicate repeated labels and prioritize the reason that adds context.
acceptance: A card’s secondary text adds new information instead of repeating its title.

area: Today list and follow-up discovery
title: One expanded card consumes most of a phone screen
observation: At 390×844, the first draft and its controls dominate the viewport and the next person is mostly below the bottom navigation.
recommendation: Provide a compact scan mode while retaining a clear focused-work mode.
acceptance: Users can review several upcoming people quickly and deliberately expand one draft.

area: Today list and follow-up discovery
title: Overdue work has weak prioritization controls
observation: The list identifies overdue items but filters do not expose relationship priority or an agreed-next-step view.
recommendation: Offer a clear overdue/priority view based on existing contact state.
acceptance: Users with a backlog can identify urgent commitments without opening every contact.

area: Today list and follow-up discovery
title: Caught-up state favors adding people
observation: The unfiltered empty state links to Add a person even if the account already has contacts and future work.
recommendation: Offer review-upcoming and schedule-existing-contact actions alongside adding someone new.
acceptance: Both an empty account and a caught-up account receive an appropriate next step.

area: Message editing, handoff, completion and outcomes
title: Open, send and complete remain separate mental steps
observation: The app opens a native composer, while Done records user-reported completion. The small control cluster can obscure that difference.
recommendation: Use clear visible labels and a concise return prompt that describes the recorded action.
acceptance: Users do not interpret opening the composer as proof a message was sent.

area: Message editing, handoff, completion and outcomes
title: Collapsed cards still expose Done and Skip
observation: A person can record completion from a collapsed card before inspecting the message or recipient.
recommendation: Test a deliberate quick-complete pattern with an explicit summary and easy correction.
acceptance: Users can tell which beat and recipient they are completing without opening unrelated menus.

area: Message editing, handoff, completion and outcomes
title: Delivery mode is not a persistent visual anchor
observation: Manual review and optional automation affect behavior across the app, while daily action cards emphasize the channel.
recommendation: Show a concise, state-derived manual/automatic/held indicator where the distinction affects an action.
acceptance: A user can identify what will happen without opening settings.

area: Message editing, handoff, completion and outcomes
title: The outcome step can add repeated work
observation: After a native handoff, users must return and record what happened; this is necessary but interruption-prone.
recommendation: Keep the return action compact, preserve the pending attempt and make later completion discoverable.
acceptance: An interrupted user can find and resolve an unrecorded handoff on returning.

area: Message editing, handoff, completion and outcomes
title: Real external-app handoffs remain a release gate
observation: No real SMS, WhatsApp, phone or email app was opened in this audit. Emulated browser behavior cannot establish recipient/body fidelity.
recommendation: Run physical-device checks with controlled recipients, including cancel, return, emoji, line breaks and long messages.
acceptance: Record successful and canceled handoffs on supported iPhone/Android combinations before public readiness signoff.

area: Contacts list, tags, filters and bulk actions
title: Select all means only the loaded page
observation: The server loads 50 contacts; toggleAll operates on that page’s contacts, while the action says Select all.
recommendation: Label it Select this page and provide a separate explicit all-results action if needed.
acceptance: With more than 50 results, the selected scope and count are unmistakable before a bulk action.

area: Contacts list, tags, filters and bulk actions
title: Out-of-range contact pages are not clamped to the result count
observation: Contacts caps the page at 10,000 but queries before reconciling it with the number of matching results.
recommendation: Clamp or redirect stale pagination when filters or deletions reduce the result set.
acceptance: A stale page URL does not present a misleading empty contact list when matching people exist.

area: Contacts list, tags, filters and bulk actions
title: Sorting cannot reflect the user’s current task
observation: The list is ordered by displayName/id; users can filter priority but cannot choose recent activity or next follow-up ordering.
recommendation: Offer a small set of useful sorts, preserving the choice with saved views.
acceptance: Users can review the most urgent or recently active relationships without scanning alphabetically.

area: Contacts list, tags, filters and bulk actions
title: Important contact tools are difficult to discover
observation: Import, duplicate review, archive and tag management sit under the generic More tools sheet.
recommendation: Label the tool entry clearly and surface the most common acquisition action in an empty or new account.
acceptance: A novice finds import and duplicate review without opening unrelated settings.

area: Contacts list, tags, filters and bulk actions
title: Contact rows emphasize methods more than next commitments
observation: The phone view prioritizes name, phone, email and More, with little visible next-action context.
recommendation: Show a concise next commitment or no-follow-up state in the scan row.
acceptance: Users can identify contacts needing a next step from the list itself.

area: Create and edit a contact
title: A recoverable validation error clears the draft
observation: Entering a name and invalid phone then saving returned Invalid phone number and blanked both fields.
recommendation: Return field errors and preserve the user’s draft instead of redirecting to an empty create form.
acceptance: An invalid phone can be corrected with every other entered value intact.

area: Create and edit a contact
title: Leaving an edited contact loses unsaved work without warning
observation: Changed Sarah’s first name, followed Back to Contact, and returned. No discard prompt appeared and the edit was gone.
recommendation: Track dirty fields and provide discard protection for navigation and reload, or a safe recoverable draft.
acceptance: Accidental navigation does not silently discard contact edits.

area: Create and edit a contact
title: Required identity is not explained beside the fields
observation: First name and last name have neither required markers nor a visible either-name rule, leaving server validation to explain an empty identity.
recommendation: State the minimum identity requirement and validate it where the user enters it.
acceptance: A user understands which combinations of name/company are accepted before submitting.

area: Create and edit a contact
title: Saving has no visible pending state
observation: ContactForm’s create/update buttons do not use the pending component.
recommendation: Disable repeat submit and show Saving with stable layout.
acceptance: A throttled save provides immediate feedback and produces one intended contact change.

area: Create and edit a contact
title: The privacy meaning of Note changes across forms
observation: Quick create labels publicNotes as Note; edit explains that it can appear in messages if a placeholder is used and offers a separate Private note.
recommendation: Make privacy visible at first capture and default sensitive relationship context appropriately.
acceptance: Users can distinguish reusable message context from private notes before saving.

area: Create and edit a contact
title: Removing a populated contact method is immediate
observation: Remove changes the in-memory email/phone/address array without an undo affordance.
recommendation: Provide undo for row removal or preserve removed values until a deliberate save review.
acceptance: Accidentally removing a populated method can be reversed without retyping it.

area: Contact detail, relationship controls and timeline
title: Older history disappears behind an undocumented cap
observation: The activity endpoint returns at most 150 combined items; the timeline has no older-items cursor or load-more control.
recommendation: Add pagination and show the range currently displayed.
acceptance: A contact with more than 150 events can reach its oldest retained history.

area: Contact detail, relationship controls and timeline
title: Timeline filter state is visual only
observation: All, Communications and Notes change class names without aria-pressed or an equivalent selected-state semantic.
recommendation: Expose the selected filter programmatically.
acceptance: Keyboard and screen-reader users can identify the active timeline view.

area: Contact detail, relationship controls and timeline
title: An empty filtered timeline gives the wrong explanation
observation: Every empty result uses No history yet, including when another filter contains events.
recommendation: Distinguish no history from no events matching this filter.
acceptance: Switching to Notes on a communications-only contact explains the filter result accurately.

area: Contact detail, relationship controls and timeline
title: Saved notes have no correction interface
observation: The visible timeline provides add and filter controls but no edit/remove action for a mistaken note.
recommendation: Provide a permission-appropriate correction or amendment workflow with preserved provenance.
acceptance: A typo or accidentally entered private detail can be corrected through a clear user-facing process.

area: Contact detail, relationship controls and timeline
title: Do not contact needs a clearer impact explanation
observation: The relationship panel says it stops future follow-ups; it does not preview the affected work beside the change.
recommendation: Show affected pending steps and explain what remains in history before saving.
acceptance: Users understand whether existing drafts, reminders and manual contact buttons remain available.

area: Contact import and recovery
title: Import polling can fail silently
observation: The 1.5-second poll has no network exception handler; non-OK responses simply return. The screen can continue claiming the import is running with stale progress.
recommendation: Show disconnected/stale status, last successful check and a retry path; stop treating stale data as live.
acceptance: Offline and 401/500 polling failures visibly change state without losing the batch identity.

area: Contact import and recovery
title: Cancel failures have no user feedback
observation: cancelBatch only handles response.ok and leaves failures or rejected fetches unexplained.
recommendation: Track cancellation pending/success/failure and preserve accurate server status.
acceptance: A failed cancellation is visibly reported and can be retried safely.

area: Contact import and recovery
title: Retry failed rows depends on the original tab state
observation: The retry button requires table, which is only in React state. Reopening an old batch can show errors without offering the same retry workflow.
recommendation: Support a server-held retry source or explicitly guide users to reselect the matching file.
acceptance: After reload, a failed batch still has an understandable recovery route.

area: Contact import and recovery
title: Clean rows are summarized without enough spot-checking
observation: The review primarily renders issue rows and aggregate counts; clean imports can proceed without a visible sample of the final records.
recommendation: Show representative mapped records and key destination fields before queueing.
acceptance: Users can catch incorrect but technically valid column mappings before records are written.

area: Contact import and recovery
title: Progress has no accessible name
observation: The results section renders a bare progress element followed by text, without an associated label.
recommendation: Name the progress control and announce material progress changes without reading the entire result panel repeatedly.
acceptance: Assistive technology identifies what is progressing and its current completion level.

area: Duplicates, archive and custom contact fields
title: Keeping the second duplicate always fails
observation: The rendered page’s hidden sourceContactId stays fixed. Selecting the second survivor submits the same ID twice; the server rejects it. The reactive DuplicateMergeForm component exists but is not used here.
recommendation: Use the reactive merge form or submit both candidate IDs and derive the source from the chosen survivor.
acceptance: Both survivor choices merge successfully and retain the intended record.

area: Duplicates, archive and custom contact fields
title: Duplicate coverage silently stops at 10,000 contacts
observation: The query takes the first 10,000 contacts, yet the empty-state copy broadly says no active contacts share details.
recommendation: Paginate candidate generation or disclose the reviewed range and remaining work.
acceptance: A larger address book never receives an all-clear based on a partial scan.

area: Duplicates, archive and custom contact fields
title: Merge does not preview conflicting values
observation: The comparison shows a short contact summary and counts, while actual field precedence is implemented server-side.
recommendation: Display the resulting primary details and conflicts before confirmation.
acceptance: Users can predict which conflicting company, custom field and primary contact method will survive.

area: Duplicates, archive and custom contact fields
title: Archive restore lacks a scheduling-impact preview
observation: Restore contact is an immediate action; the page emphasizes retained history rather than the pending-work consequences.
recommendation: Explain and summarize the resulting active assignments and future follow-ups.
acceptance: A restored contact’s next actions match the expectations shown before or immediately after restoring.

area: Duplicates, archive and custom contact fields
title: Custom field deletion does not show dependent Mixes
observation: Deletion warns about saved values and future blanks, but shows no list of templates or Mixes using that placeholder.
recommendation: Preview dependent messages and provide a replacement path before irreversible removal.
acceptance: A user can repair affected drafts/Mixes without discovering blank fields during a later send.

area: My Mixes, ready-made library and use-template setup
title: Audience preview double-counts overlapping tags
observation: Selecting Estimates and Referrals for one person showed 2 people and 4 follow-ups for a two-beat template.
recommendation: Count the distinct recipient union and derive the projection from actual eligible steps.
acceptance: One person in two selected tags counts once in both preview and activation.

area: My Mixes, ready-made library and use-template setup
title: A template draft cannot be created without an audience
observation: Create my remix is disabled when no audience is selected, including Keep as a draft. This blocks trying a template before importing people.
recommendation: Allow a draft with no audience; require a valid audience only when the relevant activation mode needs one.
acceptance: A new account can create and edit a template draft before selecting recipients.

area: My Mixes, ready-made library and use-template setup
title: New users face an undifferentiated library
observation: The seeded library contains 40 choices and initially presents relationship-themed names and framework labels.
recommendation: Offer a small set of task-based starting points using the user’s stated purpose, with the full library available.
acceptance: A novice finds a suitable first plan without understanding sales-framework terminology.

area: My Mixes, ready-made library and use-template setup
title: Using a template is hidden inside its preview
observation: Cards offer Preview the rhythm; Remix it appears inside the sheet.
recommendation: Test a direct use/create-draft action alongside preview.
acceptance: Users who have already chosen a plan can start setup without an unnecessary modal step.

area: My Mixes, ready-made library and use-template setup
title: Count and duration wording lacks edge-case polish
observation: The library visibly renders 1 beats and 0 days on a single immediate message.
recommendation: Pluralize counts and describe immediate/single-step plans naturally.
acceptance: One-step plans read as one beat or a single follow-up, with an intelligible timing summary.

area: Mix editor, timing, sequence and activation
title: A long custom plan has no unsaved-draft protection
observation: MixEditor keeps messages and sequence in component state, with a normal Cancel link and no leave/reload protection.
recommendation: Provide a recoverable draft or dirty-navigation protection consistent with the admin editor.
acceptance: Leaving or reloading a modified multi-beat plan cannot silently discard all work.

area: Mix editor, timing, sequence and activation
title: Editor activation repeats the overlapping-tag count error
observation: audienceEstimate sums group.contactCount and can overstate the number of unique people; missing-method warnings use whole-workspace counts.
recommendation: Use recipient-scoped deduplicated counts and eligibility warnings.
acceptance: The review describes the selected audience rather than unrelated contacts or repeated tag memberships.

area: Mix editor, timing, sequence and activation
title: Removing a beat loses its contents immediately
observation: removeStep filters the sequence in memory, with no undo or confirmation for a populated beat.
recommendation: Add undo or confirm removal of nonempty beats.
acceptance: A mistaken removal restores the full message, variants and timing.

area: Mix editor, timing, sequence and activation
title: Relative timing is hard to verify as actual dates
observation: The editor combines days after start, appointment anchors, offsets and advanced settings without one concrete recipient timeline.
recommendation: Add a worked schedule preview using a selected start/appointment and timezone.
acceptance: Users can verify the exact sequence dates before activation, including weekend and quiet-hour effects.

area: Mix editor, timing, sequence and activation
title: Advanced timing language increases the learning burden
observation: Cue, Tempo, Timing and several appointment anchors are presented in the authoring flow.
recommendation: Start with plain When and Message controls; reveal appointment-specific choices as needed.
acceptance: A first-time user can create a two-step plan without decoding brand terminology.

area: Member invitations and System Mix
title: Revocation is immediate despite a permanent allowance cost
observation: Revoke invitation is a direct form submit. The page says revoking does not restore an invitation slot.
recommendation: Confirm the specific recipient, link invalidation and nonrefundable slot before revoking.
acceptance: Users cannot accidentally revoke a still-needed invitation with one tap.

area: Member invitations and System Mix
title: Preparing an invitation consumes a scarce slot before sending
observation: The form explains this in a paragraph, but preparation can feel like a reversible draft step.
recommendation: Add a review summary that makes the slot cost and recipient explicit.
acceptance: Users correctly predict the remaining allowance before confirming preparation.

area: Member invitations and System Mix
title: The combined address input offers no channel-specific keyboard
observation: Email address or text number is one text input with no email/tel inputMode.
recommendation: Offer a lightweight channel choice or explicit email/phone entry modes.
acceptance: Phones expose a suitable keyboard and validation matches the selected invitation channel.

area: Member invitations and System Mix
title: Saved-contact choice is capped and requires a separate search submit
observation: Only 50 matching contacts are loaded; search refreshes the page separately from the invitation form.
recommendation: Use a searchable recipient selector that preserves in-progress invitees.
acceptance: Finding another recipient does not discard an invitation draft or hide matching people without explanation.

area: Member invitations and System Mix
title: Status has no direct link to the exact prepared reminder
observation: The invitation list says Ready in Today or Reminder skipped, while navigation goes to the overall Today list.
recommendation: Link each invitation to its specific reminder and provide a clear way to resume an unsent introduction.
acceptance: An owner reaches the correct prepared invitation without searching unrelated beats.

area: Customer journey and stage/rule configuration
title: Selecting a stage drops an existing person search
observation: Stage links on /journey rebuild the URL with only stage, while the separate search form carries q.
recommendation: Preserve compatible search criteria when changing stage filters.
acceptance: Searching then changing stage retains the query and shows clear active-filter state.

area: Customer journey and stage/rule configuration
title: Automatic and Paused are ambiguous at the person level
observation: Journey cards use a single status based on global and per-person automation, without saying which rule or pause caused it.
recommendation: Show a concise reason and a direct link to the controlling setting.
acceptance: A user can explain why one contact is paused and how to resume the intended behavior.

area: Customer journey and stage/rule configuration
title: Time in stage is not connected to a next action
observation: Cards show days in stage but offer no useful interpretation or due next commitment.
recommendation: Add an actionable next-step summary where reliable data exists.
acceptance: The board helps decide who needs attention, not only where they are categorized.

area: Customer journey and stage/rule configuration
title: Rules need a worked customer example
observation: Settings expose stages and triggers, but a nontechnical owner must mentally simulate what a milestone will do.
recommendation: Provide a dry-run example explaining stage changes and Mix activation for a selected event.
acceptance: An owner can preview the consequence of a rule without changing a live customer.

area: Customer journey and stage/rule configuration
title: Combined automation needs scenario-based usability checks
observation: The populated configuration and board were viewed, but every combination of manual holds, stage rules, appointments and Mix stops was not exercised.
recommendation: Run controlled multi-rule journeys with explicit expected behavior and explainability checks.
acceptance: Conflicting or paused automation produces a clear, recoverable user-facing state.

area: Calendar, event editor and connected availability
title: Empty calendar days create a long mobile detour
observation: Seven No time reserved sections precede the event editor. The top Schedule an event anchor helps, but the default view is still long.
recommendation: Compact empty days and provide a clear focused event-entry view.
acceptance: Users can scan availability and start an event without traversing repeated empty panels.

area: Calendar, event editor and connected availability
title: Timezone entry differs from the rest of the product
observation: The event form uses a free-text timezone with a short datalist rather than the shared searchable TimezonePicker.
recommendation: Reuse the same timezone control and show the event’s actual timezone explicitly.
acceptance: Users can select any supported zone without memorizing an IANA identifier.

area: Calendar, event editor and connected availability
title: Calendar display ignores saved locale preferences
observation: The page formats dates with Intl.DateTimeFormat("en", ...) rather than the account’s display preferences.
recommendation: Use the shared display-format helpers for calendar dates and times.
acceptance: Changing locale affects calendar formatting consistently with Today and account screens.

area: Calendar, event editor and connected availability
title: Sharing the event is explained only near Save
observation: The form eventually says saving sends no invitation and requires a calendar download to share.
recommendation: State the sharing contract near the action and provide a clear post-save handoff.
acceptance: Users do not believe the attendee was notified merely because the event was saved.

area: Calendar, event editor and connected availability
title: The event limit offers the wrong recovery direction
observation: At 500 events the page asks users to disconnect unused calendars instead of offering paging or a narrower range.
recommendation: Provide explicit truncation, filtering and range controls before suggesting disconnection.
acceptance: A busy account can inspect all relevant events without dismantling a calendar connection.

area: Lead connections and hosted inquiry form
title: Connection setup becomes technical abruptly
observation: The existing-source path asks owners to configure HTTP POST, headers, keys and JSON in another tool.
recommendation: Separate a simple hosted-form path from a clearly labeled technical connector path with worked provider instructions.
acceptance: A nontechnical owner can publish a usable lead form without encountering API setup.

area: Lead connections and hosted inquiry form
title: Recent inquiry timestamps ignore account locale
observation: Receipts are printed with toISOString and UTC, unlike customer-facing local dates elsewhere.
recommendation: Use account display preferences and preserve explicit timezone information.
acceptance: An owner can match a recent inquiry to their local working day without converting UTC.

area: Lead connections and hosted inquiry form
title: Needs-review work is a sequential ten-item queue
observation: Only the ten oldest held receipts are shown, requiring users to process them to reveal later entries.
recommendation: Add search/filter/pagination while preserving deliberate duplicate decisions.
acceptance: An owner can find an urgent held inquiry without first resolving unrelated entries.

area: Lead connections and hosted inquiry form
title: Hosted-form receipt ends without a useful next action
observation: Success says the request was received and the business can follow up, without a correction route or business return link.
recommendation: Provide a business return/contact path and clarify how to correct supplied details.
acceptance: Someone who entered a wrong phone number can understand how to correct the request.

area: Lead connections and hosted inquiry form
title: Required contact-method validation is indirect
observation: Email and phone are individually optional; the paragraph explains that one is needed, but there is no immediate combined field state.
recommendation: Validate the either-email-or-phone requirement inline and preserve all other values on failure.
acceptance: Submitting neither method moves the user directly to the relevant fields with a clear instruction.

area: Private feedback, public reviews and referrals
title: Low-score users receive fewer follow-on choices
observation: Submitting 2/5 produced a private thank-you only. The component offers public review/referral links only for the happy outcome.
recommendation: Offer a consistent, voluntary public-feedback opportunity independent of score.
acceptance: High- and low-rating users can access the same optional public-review route.

area: Private feedback, public reviews and referrals
title: Star values have no visible meaning anchors
observation: The form shows five stars and accessible numeric labels but little visible explanation of the scale endpoints.
recommendation: Label the endpoints and the selected rating in plain language.
acceptance: Users consistently understand which end represents a poor or excellent experience.

area: Private feedback, public reviews and referrals
title: Feedback cannot be corrected after submission
observation: Successful submission replaces the form with a thank-you state; there is no visible correction path.
recommendation: Provide an appropriate edit window or a clear way to contact the business about a mistake.
acceptance: An accidental rating or text error has a discoverable remedy.

area: Private feedback, public reviews and referrals
title: Private acknowledgement implies a response without setting expectations
observation: The low-score receipt says the business can make things right, but gives no contact route or next-step explanation.
recommendation: State what was recorded and provide a direct business contact option when available.
acceptance: A dissatisfied customer has a useful next step without an invented response-time promise.

area: Private feedback, public reviews and referrals
title: Real recipient comprehension is unverified
observation: The form was exercised with synthetic tokens and a low score; no customer feedback study or real follow-up was conducted.
recommendation: Test neutral invitation wording, mobile completion and understanding of private versus public feedback.
acceptance: Customers understand where their feedback goes before submitting it.

area: Business profile, personal preferences and date types
title: Timezone and schedule are separated from business setup
observation: The business page edits signatures; timezone and quiet hours live in personal preferences; automatic sending is elsewhere.
recommendation: Connect these pages with a coherent setup summary and direct links to related controls.
acceptance: Users can see the active signature, timezone and sending defaults before starting a plan.

area: Business profile, personal preferences and date types
title: Signature editing has no rendered message example
observation: Text and email signatures are edited as fields without an adjacent realistic message preview.
recommendation: Show a compact example using the current signature and a fictional recipient.
acceptance: A user can spot duplicate names, awkward spacing and overly long signoffs before saving.

area: Business profile, personal preferences and date types
title: Scheduling changes have no concrete impact preview
observation: Default time, weekend policy and quiet hours are configurable, but their combined effect is left to the user to infer.
recommendation: Show one worked next-follow-up example and explain whether existing scheduled work changes.
acceptance: The user can predict the time/date of an affected beat before confirming new defaults.

area: Business profile, personal preferences and date types
title: Customer settings forms lack consistent pending/dirty states
observation: These ordinary server-action forms do not share the admin editor’s retained-draft and submit feedback.
recommendation: Apply a consistent pending, saved, error and unsaved-changes pattern to settings.
acceptance: Slow saves and accidental navigation do not leave users unsure whether edits were kept.

area: Business profile, personal preferences and date types
title: Date types expose taxonomy before explaining consequences
observation: New custom type and active-selection controls do not show which Mixes depend on each type.
recommendation: Show usage and a simple example of adding a date to a person.
acceptance: Users know what disabling a type changes and which existing plans depend on it.

area: Notification preferences and automatic sending
title: Unavailable-email fallback can recommend unavailable push
observation: With both intentionally disabled in the audit fixture, the page said You can use push reminders instead and then Web Push is not configured.
recommendation: Compose the fallback from actual available capabilities.
acceptance: When both channels are unavailable, the page gives one accurate explanation and useful support action.

area: Notification preferences and automatic sending
title: Device reminder failure language is technical
observation: The unconfigured push state refers to Web Push and this server, rather than what the member can do.
recommendation: Use customer-facing availability wording and a relevant support route.
acceptance: The message describes a product capability and next step without server jargon.

area: Notification preferences and automatic sending
title: Email reminder preferences do not show a sample or test action
observation: The form configures morning/weekly mail and hour but has no visible preview/test counterpart to push’s test notification.
recommendation: Offer a privacy-safe preview and controlled test where delivery is configured.
acceptance: Members can verify the reminder’s contents and destination before relying on it.

area: Notification preferences and automatic sending
title: Enabling automation lacks an exact near-term sending preview
observation: The page explains the review window and requires acknowledgement, but does not list the eligible messages that will send next.
recommendation: Preview the immediate affected queue and provide a clear stop/hold path.
acceptance: Before enabling automation, the owner can identify recipients and earliest send times.

area: Notification preferences and automatic sending
title: Reminder delivery and timing need real-channel evidence
observation: Mail, SMS workers and push delivery were disabled deliberately. This audit cannot establish actual receipt or device notification behavior.
recommendation: Verify configured staging channels, quiet hours, expired sessions and permission denial using controlled recipients/devices.
acceptance: Document actual delivered reminders and accurate failure feedback before declaring these functions ready.

area: Account profile, security, export and deletion
title: Account email is displayed without a change/recovery path
observation: Profile lists email and verification status, while preferences edit name/locale/timezone only.
recommendation: Provide a verified email-change process or an explicit supported assistance route.
acceptance: A member who is losing access to an email address can find the approved way to update it.

area: Account profile, security, export and deletion
title: Social-only account deletion requires creating a password
observation: AccountDeletionForm directs users without a password to set one before deleting.
recommendation: Support equivalent recent reauthentication through the account’s available sign-in method.
acceptance: A social-only member can delete after secure reauthentication without inventing a new credential.

area: Account profile, security, export and deletion
title: Deletion warning reference points to no matching element
observation: The deletion form has aria-describedby="account-deletion-warning", but the rendered account page does not define that ID.
recommendation: Give the actual warning that ID or reference the existing warning correctly.
acceptance: The form’s accessible description includes the deletion consequences.

area: Account profile, security, export and deletion
title: Data export begins as a bare download action
observation: Spreadsheet bundle and Complete JSON links do not show size, preparation state or a customer-friendly failure recovery.
recommendation: Explain bundle contents and provide visible progress/error feedback for larger exports.
acceptance: A user can distinguish a started download, an export failure and a complete export.

area: Account profile, security, export and deletion
title: Session rows emphasize technical identifiers
observation: Rows include browser description, IP and dates but no friendly device label or obvious current-device explanation beyond the badge.
recommendation: Prioritize recognizable device/time/location context only where reliable, with technical details secondary.
acceptance: A member can identify the session they intend to revoke without interpreting an IP address.

area: Help, support requests and customer conversations
title: Customer support drafts lack the admin reply protections
observation: New-ticket and customer-reply forms are ordinary server-action forms; the admin composer retains in-tab drafts and shows pending state.
recommendation: Give customers comparable draft preservation and submit feedback.
acceptance: A network error or navigation interruption does not erase a long explanation.

area: Help, support requests and customer conversations
title: Reply expectations are unclear
observation: The support form describes what to include, but does not state an expected service window or availability.
recommendation: Publish an honest support-hours/response expectation, even if it is explicitly best effort.
acceptance: A customer knows whether to wait, check the ticket or use another channel.

area: Help, support requests and customer conversations
title: Successful FAQ filtering is not announced
observation: The FAQ result count is a visual span; only the zero-result state uses role=status.
recommendation: Announce updated result counts without moving focus from search.
acceptance: Screen-reader users hear how many answers match after changing the query.

area: Help, support requests and customer conversations
title: Tickets rely on a user’s manual description of context
observation: The form asks which page they were on but does not provide a reviewable, privacy-safe page/browser context summary.
recommendation: Offer explicit opt-in inclusion of current route and coarse technical context.
acceptance: Support receives useful reproduction context without collecting private contact data.

area: Help, support requests and customer conversations
title: No-match help sends users to a vague location
observation: The empty FAQ state says to use the help option below rather than linking directly to support.
recommendation: Offer a clear Message support link that carries the search topic only when appropriate.
acceptance: A failed help search has one obvious continuation without scrolling through the rest of the page.

area: Admin overview and navigation
title: Mobile administration uses two navigation layers
observation: A collapsed Administration menu sits above area tabs; the hierarchy and current area take substantial space before work begins.
recommendation: Keep the current location explicit and reduce repeated labels while retaining all destinations.
acceptance: An operator identifies the current area and reaches an adjacent task quickly on a phone.

area: Admin overview and navigation
title: Overflowing tab strips give little continuation cue
observation: On the mobile library screen, the Library options label is cut at the edge of the horizontally scrolling area tabs.
recommendation: Add a visible overflow cue and scroll the selected tab into view.
acceptance: All sibling destinations are discoverable and the active one is fully visible at 320 pixels.

area: Admin overview and navigation
title: Attention cards lack a common urgency scale
observation: Invitation blockers, stale monitoring and support replies share the attention list without a consistent severity/age display.
recommendation: Present consequence, urgency and age consistently while preserving direct workflow links.
acceptance: Operators can decide the first action without opening each attention item.

area: Admin overview and navigation
title: Overview freshness is a render timestamp
observation: The overview displays Updated from new Date() but has no shared refresh control or observed-data freshness explanation.
recommendation: Separate page-load time from source observation time and provide deliberate refresh.
acceptance: A long-open overview makes stale metrics apparent rather than implying they are current.

area: Admin overview and navigation
title: Staff and customer context can be easy to confuse
observation: The overview Accounts total explicitly includes staff, while admission uses a different customer-oriented capacity definition.
recommendation: Make metric naming and links clearly distinguish operational account totals from customer capacity.
acceptance: An operator does not use the overview total as the number of remaining customer places.

area: Admin account search and account controls
title: Search results provide limited triage context
observation: Rows emphasize account identity, status and session count; the operator must open an account to understand many support circumstances.
recommendation: Surface the most useful verified triage indicators, with a compact reason/status summary.
acceptance: A support operator can identify the likely target without repeatedly opening similar accounts.

area: Admin account search and account controls
title: Access changes need a task-specific review summary
observation: Suspend account and End all sessions share an operation form and generic Apply account change action.
recommendation: Show the selected operation in the submit label and a concise affected-state review.
acceptance: The operator can name the exact account and consequence immediately before submitting.

area: Admin account search and account controls
title: Suspension consequences are a dense paragraph
observation: Sessions, reminders, sending and unused referrals have different recovery behavior after suspension.
recommendation: Present an easy-to-scan consequence summary beside the selected operation.
acceptance: Operators can explain what restoring access will and will not automatically restore.

area: Admin account search and account controls
title: Session dates are not a recognizable device inventory
observation: Admin account details expose session counts/dates; identifying a particular device still requires interpretation.
recommendation: Provide a concise, privacy-appropriate device/session summary and clear current-session context.
acceptance: An operator can discuss the relevant session accurately with the account owner.

area: Admin account search and account controls
title: Denied and changing-access states need operator task checks
observation: The audit used a local Owner fixture; it did not repeat every screen under all staff roles or a live permission change.
recommendation: Run the existing role-boundary journeys alongside moderated denied-state tasks.
acceptance: A denied action explains the supported next step and preserves appropriate nonsecret draft work.

area: Admin support queue and case work
title: Queue age is time since any activity
observation: The queue displays hours since activity, which is not necessarily the time the customer has been waiting for a staff reply.
recommendation: Distinguish customer wait time from last activity and use the relevant measure for triage.
acceptance: An internal update cannot make an overdue customer reply appear newly received.

area: Admin support queue and case work
title: Reply action and email delivery need clearer separation
observation: The composer says Send reply, while helper text says the ticket is saved and email queues separately.
recommendation: Use a post-submit receipt that explicitly states saved-to-ticket and email status.
acceptance: An operator can confirm the customer-visible reply without assuming inbox delivery.

area: Admin support queue and case work
title: Reply drafts are lost on refresh
observation: The admin composer explicitly keeps the draft only in the current tab and warns that reloading discards it.
recommendation: Provide a protected save-draft mechanism or a strong reload guard consistent with the privacy model.
acceptance: Routine refresh during case investigation cannot silently remove a lengthy reply.

area: Admin support queue and case work
title: View-only support entry requires careful discovery
observation: The case page groups assignment and support-view controls in separate disclosures.
recommendation: Show a clear next permitted action when a case is unassigned or a support view is unavailable.
acceptance: A support operator can determine why view-only access is unavailable without trial and error.

area: Admin support queue and case work
title: Concurrent case handling was not qualified in this audit
observation: A synthetic case was viewed from customer and admin sides; full concurrent assignment, session expiry and real notification flows were not rerun.
recommendation: Exercise the existing support-case suite with two operators and a customer, plus controlled delivery.
acceptance: Conflicts, ended support views and failed email remain understandable and recoverable.

area: Admin waitlist, invitations and admission
title: Access status is distributed across three pages
observation: Waitlist eligibility, invitation state and admission policy must be combined mentally to understand why a person cannot join.
recommendation: Provide a linked explanation chain from a recipient to eligibility, reservation, delivery and redemption state.
acceptance: An operator can diagnose one blocked signup without losing recipient context.

area: Admin waitlist, invitations and admission
title: Capacity terminology is easy to overgeneralize
observation: The admission page explains that ceilings govern waitlist email grants while personal invitations use separate allowances. The large capacity number does not communicate that distinction alone.
recommendation: Label the number with its scope and show separate referral readiness beside it.
acceptance: Operators do not assume zero displayed capacity blocks every form of account admission.

area: Admin waitlist, invitations and admission
title: Pause controls have materially different effects
observation: Collection, new grants, referrals and redemption can be paused separately; queued messages and issued links behave differently.
recommendation: Use a plain-language state matrix preview before saving changes.
acceptance: The operator can predict what happens to a new request, queued email and existing invitation under each change.

area: Admin waitlist, invitations and admission
title: Empty waitlist still presents selection work
observation: With no eligible entries, the fixture showed Select eligible on this page, Clear selection and Review 0 invitations.
recommendation: Collapse unavailable bulk actions into a helpful empty/readiness state.
acceptance: No-recipient views direct the operator to the blocker or next setup task rather than a zero-item workflow.

area: Admin waitlist, invitations and admission
title: Invitation search hides its supported phone search
observation: The input is labeled Recipient email, although the query searches both recipientEmail and recipientPhone.
recommendation: Label the field Email or phone and include a short example where useful.
acceptance: An operator knows a text invitation can be found by its recipient phone number.

area: Admin library drafts, invitation wording and library options
title: Published and draft labels require interpretation
observation: Library rows can simultaneously display Draft 1, Published and Version 1 without saying whether the draft differs from the live version.
recommendation: Label current publication and unpublished changes distinctly.
acceptance: A reviewer identifies what customers currently see and whether an edit awaits publication.

area: Admin library drafts, invitation wording and library options
title: Customer and staff vocabulary differs
observation: The library authoring screen uses SMS and Days after start; customer screens use Text and Tempo/Beats.
recommendation: Show a customer-language preview and standardize equivalent labels where practical.
acceptance: Editors can predict exactly how authored content is presented to members.

area: Admin library drafts, invitation wording and library options
title: Long authoring forms put review context far from editing
observation: Draft metadata, messages, placeholders and change reason form a long page on mobile; publishing is a later step.
recommendation: Provide a persistent concise validity/review summary with links to incomplete sections.
acceptance: A reviewer can locate missing fields or timing problems without rescanning the entire form.

area: Admin library drafts, invitation wording and library options
title: Library option changes lack a customer-filter preview
observation: Options can be enabled/reordered with existing values preserved, but no preview shows how hidden legacy values will appear in customer filters.
recommendation: Show representative affected library/editor states before saving.
acceptance: An editor understands which new choices disappear and how existing content remains discoverable.

area: Admin library drafts, invitation wording and library options
title: Full publish/rollback usability needs a populated edit scenario
observation: The audit inspected the list, new draft, options and wording screens; it did not publish or roll back content or capture every revision conflict.
recommendation: Use isolated versioned fixtures to test edit, compare, publish, conflict and rollback with a second editor.
acceptance: Editors can verify the live version and recover from a conflict without losing their intended changes.

area: Admin email, delivery recovery and recipient suppression
title: Provider-event history stops at the latest 30
observation: The Email page takes 30 provider events and exposes no event search/pagination there.
recommendation: Add a searchable diagnostic history or a clear deep link to the appropriate complete record.
acceptance: An older delivery incident can be investigated without relying on being in the latest 30 events.

area: Admin email, delivery recovery and recipient suppression
title: Operational terms obscure the customer consequence
observation: Generation, worker attempts, provider acceptance and suppression are useful diagnostics but need interpretation.
recommendation: Lead each case with recipient impact and the next permitted action; keep technical evidence below.
acceptance: An operator can explain whether the person should wait, use an existing link or receive a reviewed resend.

area: Admin email, delivery recovery and recipient suppression
title: Recovery navigation repeats similar destinations
observation: The Email page offers multiple invitation recovery links plus staff/support and suppression paths.
recommendation: Organize by problem and recipient, with one clear destination per task.
acceptance: A failed invitation has one obvious investigation entry rather than competing similar links.

area: Admin email, delivery recovery and recipient suppression
title: Mixed suppression reasons need a simple action summary
observation: The queue groups blocks by recipient and distinguishes provider review from recipient confirmation, while detailed rules are elsewhere.
recommendation: Summarize which active reason controls the next action and why.
acceptance: Operators do not mistake clearing one provider issue for permission to contact a opted-out recipient.

area: Admin email, delivery recovery and recipient suppression
title: Real delivery recovery remains unverified here
observation: Outbound delivery and provider webhooks were not used. Empty local queues do not establish production recovery readiness.
recommendation: Run controlled accepted/failed/uncertain/blocked email cases against staging with real provider evidence.
acceptance: The UI’s delivery statements match provider records and safe retry outcomes.

area: Admin reports, export jobs and saved observations
title: Metric interpretation is hidden behind disclosures
observation: Activation, retention and live-versus-saved caveats are correct but require opening Definitions and scope to interpret headline counts.
recommendation: Place a short denominator/time-window explanation beside each decision-critical metric.
acceptance: A reader can interpret a conversion percentage without confusing account counts, eligible cohorts or missing data.

area: Admin reports, export jobs and saved observations
title: Automatic export checking stops after eight polls
observation: AdminRefresh checks every 15 seconds up to eight times; manual refresh remains, but the automatic cycle is not restarted by that button.
recommendation: Make the stopped state actionable with explicit resume/retry behavior.
acceptance: A slow export remains easy to follow after two minutes without an apparently stalled status.

area: Admin reports, export jobs and saved observations
title: Export expiry is described mostly as an absolute time
observation: Exports are session-bound and expire after 24 hours; sign-out can remove access earlier.
recommendation: Show the relevant remaining time and session restriction beside each download.
acceptance: An operator understands whether the current download will still work after signing in elsewhere.

area: Admin reports, export jobs and saved observations
title: Live and saved reporting need a stronger visual distinction
observation: Similar reports can represent recalculated current records or saved observations with different freshness semantics.
recommendation: Keep a persistent live/saved label, observation time and definition context in the report header.
acceptance: Screenshots and exported reports retain enough context to avoid treating live totals as immutable history.

area: Admin reports, export jobs and saved observations
title: Dense real-world report states were not fully exercised
observation: The audit fixture has sparse synthetic history; long labels, missing days and hundreds of retained observations need dedicated coverage.
recommendation: Run populated reporting fixtures with empty, partial, dense and failed-export states at phone widths.
acceptance: All observations and failure recovery remain usable without horizontal page overflow or ambiguous missing values.

area: Admin operations, alerts and audit investigation
title: No jobs is not the same as a healthy system
observation: The local fixture showed zero jobs and zero healthy/stale workers; the Jobs view’s empty state simply suggests another filter.
recommendation: Tie empty operational views to an explicit health/observation summary.
acceptance: Operators can distinguish idle healthy processing from no worker evidence.

area: Admin operations, alerts and audit investigation
title: Acknowledgment is easy to confuse with resolution
observation: Acknowledging stops incident reminders while the check remains open; this distinction is mainly explanatory copy.
recommendation: Persist an acknowledged-but-unresolved state with recovery criteria beside the incident.
acceptance: Acknowledgment never looks like successful recovery or disappears from the operator’s unresolved-work view.

area: Admin operations, alerts and audit investigation
title: Alert notification history is capped without paging
observation: Operational alert notices are loaded with take:30. Older notification evidence has no list continuation on that page.
recommendation: Expose an appropriate paged history or a linked full incident record.
acceptance: An operator can review older attempts for a still-relevant incident.

area: Admin operations, alerts and audit investigation
title: Audit action names are machine-oriented
observation: Audit cards lead with stored action identifiers and provide structured before/after details in a disclosure.
recommendation: Add a human-readable action summary while preserving exact identifiers for investigation.
acceptance: Operators can describe what changed without interpreting dotted action names or raw JSON.

area: Admin operations, alerts and audit investigation
title: Audit date filters and event times use different frames
observation: Filter labels use UTC while rendered event times use account display preferences.
recommendation: Show both frames clearly or provide a consistent selectable frame for investigation.
acceptance: Events near midnight are understandable within the selected date range.

area: Admin team permissions, staff onboarding and MFA
title: Permission review is a long capability inventory
observation: The override UI shows many individual capabilities and a numeric total; understanding practical role differences takes careful reading.
recommendation: Group permissions by operator task and retain a clear added/removed summary.
acceptance: An owner can explain a proposed staff member’s effective responsibilities before saving.

area: Admin team permissions, staff onboarding and MFA
title: Owner promotion can disappear without an adjacent explanation
observation: The Owner role option is filtered out when the target has no enabled MFA.
recommendation: Explain why Owner is unavailable and link the target’s supported enrollment process.
acceptance: The owner can discover the required next step without assuming the role does not exist.

area: Admin team permissions, staff onboarding and MFA
title: Copy recovery codes has no failure handling
observation: copyRecoveryCodes awaits clipboard.writeText without catch or a manual-copy recovery message.
recommendation: Handle denied/unavailable clipboard and provide an accessible manual fallback.
acceptance: Clipboard denial leaves the recovery codes visible with clear instructions rather than an unhandled failure.

area: Admin team permissions, staff onboarding and MFA
title: Continuing after enrollment does not confirm code storage
observation: The recovery screen offers Copy recovery codes and Continue to Admin with no explicit saved-codes acknowledgment.
recommendation: Ask for a simple acknowledgement or provide an equally clear save-and-continue sequence.
acceptance: A new staff member understands codes are one-time recovery material before leaving the screen.

area: Admin team permissions, staff onboarding and MFA
title: MFA and staff invitation completion need dedicated qualification
observation: This audit used local MFA-disabled admin access for broad screen review. Enrollment code was inspected; real authenticator/recovery and staff mailbox flows were not completed.
recommendation: Run the existing MFA-enabled isolated staff suite and a controlled physical authenticator exercise.
acceptance: Enrollment, recovery, expiry and permission removal are verified before administrative readiness signoff.

area: Cross-app recovery, accessibility and browser behavior
title: Public error recovery points to authenticated destinations
observation: The global not-found page offers Go to Today and Get help, both protected routes for a signed-out visitor.
recommendation: Offer public Home/Contact recovery when no account session exists.
acceptance: A public broken link does not require signing in just to recover or ask for help.

area: Cross-app recovery, accessibility and browser behavior
title: Customer routes have no loading.tsx boundaries
observation: Only the global error file exists among loading/error conventions. Server-rendered navigation has limited route-specific progress UI.
recommendation: Add purposeful loading states for slow data-heavy routes, preserving layout and focus.
acceptance: A throttled navigation communicates its destination and loading state without appearing inert.

area: Cross-app recovery, accessibility and browser behavior
title: Authenticated shell lacks the public skip link
observation: Public marketing includes Skip to content; AppShell does not provide an equivalent visible-on-focus keyboard shortcut.
recommendation: Add a consistent skip-to-main mechanism and reliable focus destination.
acceptance: Keyboard users can bypass repeated workspace navigation in one step.

area: Cross-app recovery, accessibility and browser behavior
title: Offline copy does not distinguish saved from unsaved work
observation: The offline page reassures users that saved work will be there, but offers no guidance about in-progress local drafts.
recommendation: Explain which changes are saved and give an appropriate reconnect/draft recovery path.
acceptance: Losing connectivity does not cause users to infer that an unsaved form has been stored.

area: Cross-app recovery, accessibility and browser behavior
title: Automated accessibility success is not full product qualification
observation: Desktop/mobile Chromium scans and selected 320-pixel dark states passed. Screen readers, zoom, actual soft keyboards, Safari/Firefox and performance under load were not fully qualified.
recommendation: Complete the cross-browser/device and assistive-technology matrix, using current WCAG criteria and real tasks.
acceptance: Record keyboard, screen-reader, zoom, interruption and physical-device results; resolve blockers before unrestricted launch.
